sheet.title: Mythic Bastionland
sheet.empty: Nothing yet. Drag an item here or add one.

heraldry.title: Heraldry of {name}
heraldry.lineHint: Drag from one end to the other. Hold Shift to keep it level, upright or diagonal.
heraldry.eyedropperHint: Click the shield to take a colour from it. Alt-click does the same with any tool.
heraldry.divisionsHint: Pick a division, then click a part of the shield to paint it, and the parts matching it, in the colour in hand.
heraldry.downloadHint: Save this design to your computer, to upload again later.
heraldry.downloadFailed: The design could not be turned into a file to download.

placing.title: Placing a picture
placing.hint: Drag it to move it. Scroll over it, or use the slider, to change its size. Place it to paint it in.

charges.openHint: Place a lion, a tower, a star or another charge on the shield, in the colour in hand.
charges.title: Charges
charges.hint: Click a charge to place it on the shield in the colour in hand.
charges.credit: Drawn after public-domain heraldry books by Mathghamhain Ua Ruadháin for the Book of Traceable Heraldic Art. © 2016–2023 Matthew Simon Ryan Cavalletto, CC BY-SA 4.0.

heraldry.unreadable: That picture couldn’t be loaded onto the shield.
heraldry.tooLarge: This heraldry is too detailed to keep on the Knight. Simplify it, or ask the GM to let you upload files.

vig.label: Vigour
vig.hint: Strong limbs, firm hands, powerful lungs.

cla.label: Clarity
cla.hint: Keen instinct, lucid mind, shrewd eyes.

spi.label: Spirit
spi.hint: Charming tongue, iron will, fierce heart.

glory.label: Glory
glory.title: Glory
glory.nobody: Nobody was ticked, so no Glory is awarded.

myth.label: Myth Resolved
myth.intro: Tick every Knight who played a part in the Myth. Each gains 1 Glory.
myth.hint: When the group feels that a Myth has reached a conclusion of any type.

tournament.label: Tournament Won
tournament.intro: Tick the winning Knight. They gain 1 Glory.
tournament.hint: Only a tournament with significant spectators and spectacle grants Glory.

battle.label: Battle Won
battle.intro: Tick every Knight on the victorious side. Each gains 1 Glory.
battle.hint: Only a battle large enough to be remembered in history grants Glory.

squire.label: Squire
squire.empty: Small Companies of 2 Knights or fewer may give each Knight a Squire. Take one, or drag a Squire here from the Actors tab.
squire.servesNobody: A Squire who serves no Knight. Drag this Squire onto a Knight’s sheet.
squire.hint: An apprentice, not yet a Knight, so they can’t gain Glory or perform Feats. When Knighted they gain d6 in each Virtue.
squire.noFeats: Squires can’t perform Feats until they are Knighted.
squire.name: Squire to {knight}
squire.title: A Squire
squire.largeCompany: Only Companies of 2 Knights or fewer may give each Knight a Squire, and this one has {count}. Take a Squire anyway?
squire.cantCreate: Taking a Squire creates them and their pony, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors.
squire.knightConfirm: {name} becomes a Knight, gaining d6 in each Virtue. From then on they can gain Glory and perform Feats.

fatigued.label: Fatigued
fatigued.hint: Cannot perform Feats until they rest.

exhausted.label: Exhausted
exhausted.hint: At VIG 0 you cannot Attack if you have moved this turn.

exposed.label: Exposed
exposed.hint: Treated as having 0GD. CLA 0 also leaves you Exposed.

impaired.label: Impaired
impaired.hint: At SPI 0 your Attacks roll a single d4 only.

mortalWound.label: Mortal Wound
mortalWound.hint: Down and dying. They die if left untended for an hour, but can be patched up in a few moments.

recovery.label: Recovery
recovery.rested: A moment’s calm: GD restored to {value} and Fatigue removed.

steed.label: Steed
steed.empty: Drag an NPC from the Actors tab here to ride it. Its trample joins a mounted charge.
steed.fromDirectory: Drag the steed from the Actors tab rather than a compendium, so it can be targeted in combat.

remedy.intro: Tick everybody present. Each has their {virtue} restored, and the Remedy is used up.
remedy.hint: Using a Remedy takes a whole Phase. The Virtue is restored before any Omens or other encounters.

feats.label: Feats

smite.name: Smite
smite.summary: +d12 or Blast to a melee attack.
smite.use: Use before rolling a melee Attack. The Attack gains either +d12 or Blast.

focus.name: Focus
focus.summary: Perform a Gambit without using a die.
focus.use: Use after rolling an Attack. Perform a Gambit without using a die.

deny.name: Deny
deny.tagline: Rebuff an attack before it lands
deny.summary: Discard a damage die rolled against you or a nearby Ally.
deny.use: Use after an Attack roll against you or an ally within arm’s reach. Discard one Attack die from the roll.

feats.alreadyFatigued: {name} is Fatigued and cannot perform Feats until they rest.

gambits.label: Gambits
gambits.stop: Stop a foe from moving next turn
gambits.impair: Impair a weapon on their next turn
gambits.trap: Trap a shield until your next turn
gambits.other: Other effect of a similar level of impact
gambits.hint: Discard Attack dice of 4 or higher, one per Gambit. Foes get a VIG Save against all but Bolster and Move.
gambits.strong: Strong Gambit: a melee die of 8+ also grants No Save or a Greater effect.

morale.title: Morale
morale.hint: Roll when Wounded, or when a group loses half its number. An organised group rolls once, on its leader’s SPI.
morale.notOwner: Only a GM or {name}’s owner can roll their Morale.

triggers.wounded: {name} is Wounded, and must pass a SPI Save to avoid rout or surrender.
triggers.halved: {name} has lost half its number, and must pass a SPI Save to avoid rout or surrender.

group.title: Wavering Morale
group.intro: {down} of {count} on this side are down. The rest must pass a SPI Save to avoid rout or surrender.
group.noneStanding: Nobody you control in this group is still standing.

organised.label: Organised
organised.hint: An organised group rolls once, on its leader’s SPI.

disorganised.label: Disorganised
disorganised.hint: A disorganised group rolls for each individual, on their own SPI.

duel.title: Duel
duel.buttonHint: Target the one Token you’ve agreed to duel, then press this.
duel.needTarget: Target the one Token you’ve agreed to duel, then press Duel.
duel.intro: {name} and {opponent} agree to fight. They fight as normal, but their Attacks are rolled and resolved at the same time, including the effects of Gambits, and both can use Feats before they’re resolved.

duel.label: Duel
duel.hint: Two combatants who mutually agree to fight.

duel.stakeHint: In a public duel or joust, Knights may stake Glory against a willing opponent. The victor gains 1 Glory, and the loser loses 1.
duel.stakeKnightsOnly: Only two Knights can stake Glory, and a Squire isn’t a Knight yet.
duel.bloodlessHint: Training, or a duel that isn’t to the death. Scars only come from real, deadly combat, so it leaves none.
duel.stakeNote: Glory is staked: the victor gains 1, and the loser loses 1.
duel.bloodlessNote: Bloodless: a blow that would cause a Scar leaves none.
duel.howTo: Each duelist presses Attack on their sheet, then uses Feats and declares Gambits on their card. A GM, or whoever owns both, then resolves the two Attacks together.
duel.endedNoVictor: The duel ends without a victor.
duel.attackHint: Targets the other duelist, and holds the Damage back until both Attacks are in.
duel.heldForDuel: Part of a duel: the Damage is applied from the duel card, together with the other Attack.
duel.notReady: Both duelists need to roll their Attack first.
duel.gone: One of the duelists no longer exists.
duel.attackGone: One of the duel’s Attack cards has been deleted.
duel.cantResolve: Only a GM, or somebody who owns both duelists, can resolve their Attacks.
duel.cantEnd: Only a GM, or somebody who owns both duelists, can end the duel.
duel.noScar: {name} would take a Scar, but a bloodless duel leaves none.
duel.needsGM: A GM needs to be logged in to change somebody else’s duel card.
duel.changeRefused: The duel card changed before that could be recorded.

surprise.title: Roll Surprise
surprise.intro: Tick everybody who wasn’t readied for combat. Each makes a CLA Save or misses the first turn.
surprise.hint: Players normally take the first turn, discussing their plan and acting in any order they wish.
surprise.noCombatants: This encounter has nobody in it yet.
surprise.nobody: Nobody was caught unready, so there’s nothing to roll.

time.title: Time
time.setByHand: Click a Season or Phase, or change the Age or Day, to set the calendar by hand. Only the buttons below carry out what happens between Seasons and Ages.

phaseHints.morning: Sunrise to noon. Anybody who didn’t get proper sleep loses d6 CLA, and anybody deprived of essential needs loses d6 VIG.
phaseHints.night: Sunset to sunrise. Travelling or exploring at night costs d6 SPI each, and without a guide and light the Company travels blind.

time.seasonIntro: {season} gives way to {next}. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored and chooses a pursuit, and any Mutilation Scar settles.
time.ageIntro: Age {age} begins in Spring. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored, gains 1 Glory and chooses a pursuit. Old Knights lose d12 VIG, and any Mutilation Scar settles.
time.noCompany: There are no Knights in this world yet, and no Tokens are selected.

pilgrimage.label: Pilgrimage
pilgrimage.hint: Learn about an unknown part of the Realm.

courtesy.label: Courtesy
courtesy.hint: Establish a new contact or earn a favour.

service.label: Service
service.hint: Make a small improvement to the Realm.

duty.label: Duty
duty.hint: Make a significant improvement to the Realm.

succession.label: Succession
succession.hint: Establish a successor, or have them Knighted.

legacy.label: Legacy
legacy.hint: Your successor gains half of your current Glory.

time.oldAge: Old age: loses {amount} VIG, max VIG {from} → {to}.
time.unresolvedHint: Roll an Unresolved Situation for anything important left hanging.
time.winterReminder: It’s Winter: anybody camping or travelling at night loses d6 VIG, and dire weather may keep the Company where it is.

hardship.title: Hardship
hardship.none: Nobody was ticked, so nobody loses anything.
hardship.notDamage: Virtue Loss isn’t Damage, so it can’t Mortally Wound or Slay.

night.label: Night travel
night.hint: Travelling or exploring at night costs d6 SPI each.

sleep.label: No proper sleep
sleep.hint: Each morning, all who didn’t get proper sleep the day before lose d6 CLA.

winter.label: Winter cold
winter.hint: Camping, or travelling at night, in Winter costs d6 VIG each.

supplies.label: Deprived
supplies.hint: Each morning without essential needs met, the Company each lose d6 VIG.

aging.title: Growing Older
aging.intro: {name} becomes {age}. Roll each Virtue on d12+d6 for it?

domain.seatHint: The Holding of the ruler of the whole Realm, facing the same problems on a larger scale.

council.label: Council
council.hint: Council members can be given tasks lasting a Phase, a Week or a Season. They’re handled as normal actions, and failure usually brings a Crisis. Seats can be granted and revoked, but the scorned rarely go quietly.

steward.label: Steward
steward.hint: Rules in your absence, carrying your authority and the key to the treasury.

marshal.label: Marshal
marshal.hint: Trains and equips soldiers, and musters them in times of war.

sheriff.label: Sheriff
sheriff.hint: Watches for threats within the Realm, and within your own walls.

envoy.label: Envoy
envoy.hint: Manages neighbours, and gives hospitality to visitors.

circle.label: The Circle
circle.hint: Worthy visiting Knights invited to sit alongside the Council as equals.

chaos.name: Chaos
chaos.resolution: Resolved by enforcing a sense of justice.

debt.name: Debt
debt.flavour: dire need of coffer and coin

famine.name: Famine
famine.resolution: Resolved by getting food into the stores.

misery.name: Misery
misery.resolution: Resolved by raising the spirits of the people.

panic.name: Panic
panic.resolution: Resolved by making the Vassals feel safe.

doubt.name: Doubt
doubt.resolution: Resolved by asserting your authority to rule.

domain.crisisRollHint: Roll at the start of each Season, or on returning from a long absence.
domain.rolledThisSeason: The Crisis Roll has been made this Season ({season}).
domain.notRolledThisSeason: The Crisis Roll hasn’t been made this Season yet ({season}).

crisis.dilemma: Dilemma: a choice between two Crises.

collections.crisis: The coffers are filled, but a Crisis comes with it.

domain.dilemmaIntro: {name} must take on one of these Crises.
domain.dilemmaOpen: No choice was made between {options}. Add the one chosen from the sheet.
domain.misruleHint: Vassals revolt, Knights leave, and pretenders move in on their claims.
domain.misruleDue: {count} unresolved Crises: if the Season ends like this, the Domain falls into misrule.
domain.fellIntoMisrule: The Season ended with {count} unresolved Crises, and the Domain falls into misrule.
domain.seasonHint: Make the Crisis Roll for each Domain from its sheet.
domain.collectionsHint: A Steward squeezes more from the Vassals for a war or a great project.
domain.dramaHint: Every Season brings some drama. Roll to see how the ruler is involved.
domain.muster: Can muster {count} Warbands. The Marshal decides their training and armament.
domain.designs: Grand designs: work on existing buildings is done by next Season, a new building takes a Season, and grand projects such as castles and roads take an Age.
domain.succession: Succession: a ruler usually names their successor, though some Realms leave it to a conclave of Seers or Knights-Elector. Whoever it is faces some resistance.

goods.foldersSeeded: Arms & Goods: added {items} items to the Items directory and {actors} beasts, hirelings, Warbands and structures to the Actors directory.

spark.title: Spark Tables
spark.hint: Roll a table for a d12 in each column, and combine the two into a prompt to improvise from.
spark.noIndex: Run the Import Book Art macro with your rulebook to bring in the Spark Tables.
spark.noText: Run Import Book Art again with your rulebook to bring in the Spark Tables.
spark.pageMissing: The Spark Tables on this page couldn’t be read. Import Book Art’s report says why.

myths.title: Myths
myths.hint: Each Myth in the Realm with its six Omens, the ones seen so far marked. The Realm’s Hex panel and the Wilderness Roll count the same Omens.
myths.noRealm: There’s no Realm Scene yet. Use New Realm in the Scenes tab to roll one.

cityQuest.title: The City Quest
cityQuest.hint: A Company worthy of the City Quest meets an Omen of the City instead of a random Myth’s Omen when the Wilderness Roll is a 1. Roll d12 plus the Omens of the City already encountered, taking the next one down the list for a duplicate.
cityQuest.noText: Run Import Book Art again to quote the Omens of the City here.
cityQuest.seen: Omens of the City encountered: {count}. The City Quest ends after Omen {end} or higher.
cityQuest.roll: Roll an Omen of the City
cityQuest.ends: Omen 18 or higher: after this Omen, the City Quest ends.
cityQuest.resetConfirm: Every Omen of the City encountered is forgotten, as for a new Company.
cityQuest.wildernessHint: A Company worthy of the City Quest encounters an Omen of the City instead. Roll it from the Myths window.

sites.title: Sites
sites.hint: Map a Site the way the book does: points on the corners and centre of a hexagon, joined by routes between neighbours. The same seed and counts always draw the same Site.
sites.name: Name

feature.label: Feature
feature.hint: Gives information or sets the mood.

closed.hint: Something blocks the way, so creative thinking is required.

hidden.hint: Only found by exploring the points at either end, or through local knowledge.

sites.empty: There are no points to map.
sites.journalHint: Describe what’s found at each point beneath its entry.

problems.noPoints: A Site needs at least one point.
problems.tooManyPoints: A hexagon has room for {used} points, not {asked}.
problems.tooFewRoutes: Every point must be reachable, so there are {used} routes, not {asked}. The extra ones are open.
problems.tooManyRoutes: Only {used} routes fit between neighbouring points, not {asked}.
problems.hiddenEntrance: With only one point, there’s nowhere else to put the hidden entrance.

refereeRolls.title: Referee Rolls
refereeRolls.intro: Roll a d6 on one of the Referee’s tables. A low roll goes against the players.

luck.name: Luck Roll
luck.hint: When you need to consult the whims of fate.

results.problem: Problem: something that could turn bad.

passage.name: Passage of Time
passage.hint: At the end of a session, when it isn’t clear how much time should pass.

results.now: The Season or Age turns now.
results.afterNextSession: The Season or Age turns after the next session.
results.continues: The Season or Age carries on.

unresolved.name: Unresolved Situation
unresolved.hint: For an important situation still unresolved as the Season or Age turns.

results.worst: It goes as badly as it possibly could.

blind.name: Travelling Blind
blind.hint: When travellers without a proper sense of direction, or shrouded by darkness or mist, try to move to a new Hex.

results.circleBack: They circle back to where they started.
results.drift: They drift a Hex to the {side}.

weather.name: Dire Weather
weather.hint: At the start of each Phase in lands at the mercy of dire weather, as most Realms are in Winter.

results.dire: Dire weather: nobody can leave the Hex or get proper sleep.
results.looming: A looming threat. Rolled twice in a row, it’s dire weather.

results.woe: Troubled by a looming or recent woe.
results.decline: A sense of things in decline.
results.fine: A fine mood, and all seems well enough.

attack.title: Attack
attack.noWeapons: Nothing is worn or wielded, so this Attack is unarmed and Impaired.
attack.bonusHint: From useful information, shrewd preparations, or a tactical advantage. +d8 is typical.
attack.smiteHint: A VIG Save follows to avoid Fatigue.
attack.blastHint: Roll separately against everybody in the area.
attack.movedHint: Ticked when the Token has moved this turn in combat. Slow weapons can’t be used after moving, and an Exhausted character can’t Attack.
attack.engaged: Began the turn engaged in melee
attack.engagedHint: Purely ranged weapons can’t be used.
attack.mountedHint: A lance counts as Hefty rather than Long on horseback, so it can be wielded with a shield.
attack.spearwallHint: 3 or more allies in a wall formation, all bearing spears or similar. Enemies can’t Attack on the turn they charge it.
attack.charge: Charging on {steed} at enemies on foot (+{dice})
attack.chargeHint: A steed’s trample joins the Attack when charging enemies on foot. It doesn’t work against a spearwall.
attack.confinedImpaired: A Long weapon in a confined space is Impaired: it rolls a single d4 and gains no bonus dice or Feats.

setAside.slow: {name} is Slow, so it can’t be used after moving.
setAside.ranged: {name} is purely ranged, so it can’t be used after beginning the turn engaged in melee.

refusals.exhausted: {name} is Exhausted, so they can’t Attack after moving this turn.
refusals.spearwall: Enemies of a spearwall can’t Attack on the turn they charge it.
refusals.hefty: Only one Hefty item can be wielded at once.
refusals.long: A Long weapon needs both hands, so it can’t be wielded with anything else.

attack.impaired: Impaired: rolls a single d4 and gains no bonus dice or Feats.
attack.againstIndividualsHint: A Warband’s Attack on individuals gets +d12 and causes Blast Damage.
attack.leaderHint: One individual within the Warband adds their Attack dice to its roll, and suffers the same Damage the Warband does until their next turn. Select their Token to list them.
attack.ledBy: {name} leads from the front, suffering the same Damage as the Warband until their next turn.
attack.damageNote: Deny first, then click a die of 4+ to spend it on a Gambit. Click a spent die to take its Gambit back. The highest die left is the Damage.
attack.saveToIgnore: The target may make a VIG Save to ignore it.
attack.dismounted: Being dismounted adds a d6 showing {result} to the dice. Take the Gambit back if they Save.
attack.noDenier: Select the Token of whoever Denies, or give your User a character.
attack.featUsed: {name} has already used {feat} on this Attack.
attack.noTarget: Target the Tokens this Attack hits, then apply the Damage.
attack.targetsGone: The Tokens this Attack targeted are gone.
attack.cantApply: Only a GM or the target’s owner can apply this Damage.
attack.needsGM: A GM needs to be logged in to change somebody else’s Attack card.
attack.changeRefused: The Attack card changed before that could be recorded.

damage.title: Take Damage
damage.amountHint: The highest die left after Gambits, plus any Bolster.
damage.cover: Behind protective cover, against a ranged Attack (+1 Armour)
damage.shieldwallHint: 3 or more allies in a wall formation, all bearing shields rather than bucklers.
damage.doom: Doom: a cheated death catches up with them. Slain instead of Mortally Wounded.
damage.leaderShares: {name} leads {warband} from the front, so suffers the same {damage} Damage. Apply it from their sheet.

warband.label: A Blast or large-scale Attack
warband.hint: Individual Attacks don’t harm a Warband.

structure.label: Fire, a siege weapon or a suitably large creature

outcomes.none: The blow is turned aside. No Damage.
outcomes.scar: Left at exactly 0GD. Roll a Scar with the die that caused it.
outcomes.mortal: Mortally Wounded: down and dying. They die if left untended for an hour.

structureOutcomes.destroyed: Destroyed at 0GD. Recovering GD takes a day of repairs.

scarRoll.title: Roll Scar
scarRoll.die: The die that caused the Scar
scarRoll.apply: Record the Scar and apply its Virtue Loss and immediate GD increase
scarRoll.settle: Settle this Scar: roll its GD increase now its moment has come
scarRoll.settledRaise: {name} settles: max GD rises by {amount} to {value}.
scarRoll.settledNoRaise: {name} settles, but max GD is already above {limit}, so it doesn’t rise.

disfigurement.name: Disfigurement
disfigurement.effect: Roll d6 for where. If your max GD is 2 or less, increase it by d6.

stun.name: Stun
stun.effect: Lose d6 CLA. If your max GD is 4 or less, increase it by d6.

gouge.name: Gouge
gouge.effect: When you get stitched up, if your max GD is 6 or less, increase it by d6.

concussion.name: Concussion
concussion.flavour: A heavy blow numbs the mind

tear.name: Tear
tear.effect: Roll d6 for what. When you get patched up, if your max GD is 8 or less, increase it by d6.

agony.name: Agony
agony.flavour: With a crack, a torturous break

mutilation.name: Mutilation
mutilation.flavour: A limb rendered lost or useless
mutilation.effect: Roll d6 for which. By next Season you have a prosthetic or have learned to get by, and if your max GD is 10 or less, increase it by d6.

doom.name: Doom
doom.effect: If you take a Mortal Wound this Season you are Slain instead.

humiliation.name: Humiliation
humiliation.effect: When you achieve revenge, if your max GD is 12 or less, increase it by d6.

item.heftyHint: One hand. Only one Hefty item can be wielded at once.
item.longHint: Both hands. Impaired in confined environments.
item.slowHint: Cannot be used if the wielder moved this turn. Also Long.
item.heftyMountedHint: Counts as Hefty rather than Long when the wielder is mounted, as a lance does.
item.rangedHint: Cannot be used if the wielder began their turn engaged in melee.
item.blastHint: Attacks everybody in the area, rolled separately for each.
item.ignoresArmourHint: Damage isn’t reduced by the target’s Armour.
item.trampleHint: A steed’s trample. Its rider adds it to their Attack when charging enemies on foot.
item.remedyHint: When used, restores this Virtue to everybody present, and is used up.
item.attackDieHint: Shields strike for d4. Leave blank for armour that never attacks.

npc.name: Name

warband.label: Warband
warband.hint: Two-dozen or so fighting as one. Only Blast or large-scale Attacks harm them, and their Attacks on individuals get +d12 and Blast.

routed.label: Routed
routed.hint: A Mortal Wound routs a Warband from the battle.

broken.label: Broken
broken.hint: At SPI 0 a Warband is broken, acting only in its own interest.

wipedOut.label: Wiped Out
wipedOut.hint: At VIG 0 a Warband is wiped out entirely.

leader.label: Led from the front by {name}, who suffers the same Damage until their next turn.

npc.structureHint: Only fire, siege weapons or suitably large creatures can harm it.
npc.featsHint: Feats are for Knights, but some of the Cast can perform one. Mark the ones this character can.

paste.title: Paste Stat Block
paste.intro: Paste a stat block, such as one copied from the rulebook. It replaces this NPC’s name, Virtues, GD, Armour, Feats and notes, and swaps their weapons for its attacks.
paste.placeholder:
Name, Epithet
VIG 10, CLA 10, SPI 10, 3GD
A1 (what their Armour is)
Weapon (d8 hefty)
Anything else about them.
paste.hint: Only the VIG, CLA, SPI and GD line is needed. Text above it becomes the name.
paste.noStats: No stat line found. It should read like VIG 10, CLA 10, SPI 10, 3GD.

npcChooser.title: Choose an NPC
npcChooser.noCityQuest: Run Import Book Art again to bring in the City Quest’s Omens and Cast.
npcChooser.noIndex: Run the Import Book Art macro to see each Myth’s Cast and each Seer here.
npcChooser.noText: Run Import Book Art again to bring in each Myth’s Omens and Cast and each Seer’s Virtues.
npcChooser.noPeople: No stat blocks were read from this page.
npcChooser.noSelection: Pick a Myth or a Seer to see them here.
npcChooser.confirm: {name} becomes {npc}. Their name, picture, Virtues, GD, Armour, Feats and notes are replaced, and their weapons are swapped for these attacks. Other items are kept.

bookArt.title: Import Book Art
bookArt.intro: Choose your copy of the Mythic Bastionland rulebook, the {pages}-page PDF. Every Knight’s and Seer’s portrait and every Myth’s illustration is saved for this system to use. So is the text the choosers fill characters in from: each Knight’s Property, Ability and Passion, each Seer’s Virtues, each Myth’s Omens and Cast, and the Spark Tables. A GM also gets compendiums of the weapons, armour, gear, beasts, hirelings, Warbands and structures from Arms & Goods.
bookArt.chooseHint: The file is read in your browser and never uploaded.
bookArt.outputHint: Pictures are saved to {root} in your Foundry data folder, replacing any from an earlier import.
bookArt.notReady: Import Book Art can run once the world has finished loading.
bookArt.running: Import Book Art is already running.
bookArt.noPermission: Import Book Art saves files, so it needs a user who is allowed to upload files.
bookArt.unreadable: {name} couldn’t be opened as a PDF.
bookArt.pageMismatch: This PDF has {pages} pages, but the rulebook this import was made for has {expected}. Pictures may be missing or mixed up. Import anyway?
bookArt.layoutMismatch: The first Knight’s pages don’t have the pictures this import looks for, so this may be a different edition. Import anyway?
bookArt.progress: Import Book Art: reading page {page} of {last}
bookArt.readingSpark: Import Book Art: reading the Spark Tables
bookArt.readingGoods: Import Book Art: reading Arms & Goods
bookArt.readingCityQuest: Import Book Art: reading the City Quest
bookArt.fillingGoods: Import Book Art: filling the Arms & Goods compendiums
bookArt.writingIndex: Import Book Art: writing the index
bookArt.packMissing: Import Book Art couldn’t be added to this world because the Mythic Bastionland Macros compendium is empty. Run npm run pack with Foundry closed, then restart Foundry.

report.title: Book Art Imported
report.cityQuestRead: City Quest: {omens} of {total} Omens and {cast} of the Cast read
report.goods: Arms & Goods: {items} items in the {itemsPack} compendium, and {actors} beasts, hirelings, Warbands and structures in {actorsPack}
report.goodsNotGM: Arms & Goods were read, but only a GM can fill their compendiums. Run the import again as a GM.
report.goodsFailed: The Arms & Goods compendiums couldn’t be filled. If either is locked, unlock it and run the import again.
report.goodsFolders: Arms & Goods copied into the world: {items} new items and {actors} new NPCs, in folders named for each compendium
report.goodsFoldersFailed: Arms & Goods couldn’t be copied into the Items and Actors directories. Run the import again.
report.knightTokens: Knight tokens: {actors} Knights and {tokens} tokens on scenes now show the square cut around the Knight’s face
report.knightTokensFailed: Existing Knights couldn’t be given their square tokens. Run the import again.
report.indexFailed: The index couldn’t be saved, so the pictures can’t be looked up by roll. Run the import again.
report.unnamed: Saved without a name, because the page’s title couldn’t be read:
report.none: Every picture was found and saved.

reasons.notFound: no matching picture on the page
reasons.extra: more than one picture matched, so the largest was saved
reasons.upload: the server didn’t accept the file
reasons.text: the Knight’s Property, Ability or Passion couldn’t be read, so the chooser won’t fill them in
reasons.mythText: the Omens or Cast couldn’t be read, so the NPC chooser won’t list them
reasons.seerText: the Seer’s Virtues and traits couldn’t be read, so the NPC chooser won’t fill them in
reasons.sparkText: its rows couldn’t be read, so it’s left out of the Spark Tables
reasons.sparkPage: no Spark Tables could be read from the page
reasons.goodsKind: none could be read, so the compendium goes without them
reasons.cityQuestText: they couldn’t be read, so the City Quest goes without them

chooser.title: Choose a Knight
chooser.noIndex: Run the Import Book Art macro to see each Knight’s name, portrait, Property, Ability and Passion. You can still roll.
chooser.noText: Run Import Book Art again to bring in each Knight’s Property, Ability and Passion.

wanderer.label: Wanderer
wanderer.summary: Young Knights-Errant. Virtues d12+d6, GD d6.

courtier.label: Courtier
courtier.summary: Mature Knights-Gallant with a place in Court. Virtues d12+6, GD 2d6.

ruler.label: Ruler
ruler.summary: Mature Knights-Tenant, one ruling a Holding. Virtues d12+6, GD d6+6.

chooser.scoresHint: Rolls VIG, CLA and SPI in order, then GD, with the Start’s dice. Change a result by hand if you need to.
chooser.knightHint: Read the d6 first, then the d12. Or pick a Knight. Generally each player should have a different one.
chooser.noSelection: Roll or pick a Knight to see them here.
chooser.confirm: {name} becomes {knight}. Their Property, Ability and Passion are replaced, along with the picture in their shield, their Age, Glory and anything rolled here. Scars and the Chronicle are kept.

card.knightRoll: {d6} on the d6, {d12} on the d12

dialog.title: New Realm
dialog.intro: Rolls a Realm the way Creating a Realm describes, on a Scene of 12 by 12 hexes: terrain, a river, four Holdings, six Myths, Landmarks and Barriers.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.seedHint: The same seed rolls the same Realm.
dialog.secretHint: Players see the terrain, the river and the Holdings. Myths, Landmarks and Barriers stay hidden until you reveal them.

key.tagline: Realm Key for seed {seed}. Only GMs see this.

movement.offMap: That’s past the edge of the Realm.

wilderness.title: Wilderness Roll
wilderness.notRealm: The Wilderness Roll works on a Realm Scene.
wilderness.split: The Company is spread over more than one hex, so the roll is for {hex}, where most of them stand.
wilderness.chooseMode: How does the Company end this Phase at {hex}?

results.holding: A Holding isn’t Wilderness, so there’s no roll.
results.mythHex: In the Myth’s own hex, its next Omen shows without a roll.
results.randomOmen: An Omen from a Myth chosen at random.
results.nearestOmen: An Omen from the nearest Myth.
results.noMyths: This Realm has no Myths, so all is quiet.

wilderness.omensComplete: All of its Omens have been seen.
wilderness.tied: Myths {numbers} are equally near, so a roll chose between them.

tidy.problems: The Realm has {count} things to look at: {list}

reroll.title: Reroll the Realm?
reroll.confirm: A new Realm is rolled onto this Scene, replacing its terrain, river, Holdings, Myths, Landmarks and Barriers. Tokens and anything else on the Scene stay.

problems.crowded: More than one thing in a hex
problems.edge: A Barrier between hexes that don’t touch
problems.style: A Holding of no known style
problems.type: A Landmark of no known type
problems.seat: Not exactly one Seat of Power

panel.title: Realm
panel.missing: This Scene isn’t a Realm any more.
panel.brushHint: Choose the terrain to paint, then click or drag across hexes. Alt-click a hex to pick up its terrain.
panel.name: Name

look.title: Realm Appearance
look.hint: Choose how Realm Scenes are drawn: a skin, a set of colours, and pictures of your own.
look.intro: Try a skin and a set of colours below, then apply them. Every Realm Scene in the world is redrawn, with its paper, hex lines and Barriers in the new colours. Nothing about the Realm itself changes.

sheet.label: Blank Realm
sheet.hint: The Blank Realm sheet’s own inked terrain, Holdings and Landmarks, with rivers as the Realm Sheets draw them.

classic.label: Roundels
classic.hint: Pale hexes, fine marks and lettered roundels.

woodcut.label: Woodcut
woodcut.hint: Bold lines, shields for Holdings and Myths, signs for Landmarks.

atlas.label: Surveyor’s Atlas
atlas.hint: Soft washes, fine marks and silhouettes.

fits.icon: Terrain pictures sit inside their hex

look.ownIntro: Use pictures of your own. Name each file after the picture it replaces, such as forest.png or holding-castle.webp. Any picture you don’t give comes from the skin.
look.namesHint: Uploaded pictures are saved to {dir}. Terrain can also be named by its terrain, such as marsh or terrain-marsh; Holdings and Landmarks by their kind alone, such as tower or ruin. Any image type works. Ticked names are found.
look.ignored: {count} files weren’t uploaded: their names don’t match a Realm picture.
look.applied: Realm Scenes are being redrawn in the new look.

restoreOpenSheets.name: Reopen Sheets on Reload
restoreOpenSheets.hint: Reopen the Knight, item and journal sheets and the rulebook you had open, where you left them, when you reload Foundry. Only affects this browser.

rulebook.title: Mythic Bastionland
rulebook.nobodyToShow: No one else is signed in to show the page to.
rulebook.noCopy: The GM hasn’t given this world a copy of the rulebook yet.
rulebook.otherEdition: This PDF has {pages} pages, but the rulebook this system’s page numbers come from has {expected}, so a jump to a page may land in the wrong place.
rulebook.notPdf: That file doesn’t look like a PDF. It’s been saved anyway, in case it is one.
rulebook.copying: Copying the rulebook into the world…
rulebook.copied: The rulebook is ready to read.
rulebook.copyFailed: The rulebook couldn’t be copied into the world. Check that you’re allowed to upload files and that there’s space.
rulebook.keepFailed: The rulebook was copied in, but the world couldn’t record where it went.

keybinding.name: Open the Rulebook
keybinding.hint: Open the rulebook, or close it when it’s already in front.

forPlayers.name: Let Players Open the Rulebook
forPlayers.hint: Players get the Rulebook button and hotkey too. Pages the GM shows them open either way.

setup.title: Your Rulebook
setup.intro: Point this world at your own copy of the Mythic Bastionland PDF to read it in Foundry’s PDF viewer, with its chapters, search and page links.
setup.choose: Choose a File on This Computer
setup.copyHint: A file chosen from this computer is copied to {dir} in your Foundry data folder, so it’s still there next session. Forgetting it leaves the file there.
setup.whoCanRead: Foundry serves everything in its data folder to anyone signed into the world who knows the path, so treat the copy as shared with your table.
setup.hotkey: Press B to open or close the rulebook. Change the key under Configure Controls.
